sentences.zh: 李時勉，名懋，以字行，安福人。

translations.literal: Li Shimian, personal name Mao, was known by his style name; he was a native of Anfu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shimian, whose personal name was Mao but who went by his style name, came from Anfu.

sentences.zh: 成童時，冬寒，以衾裹足納桶中，誦讀不已。

translations.literal: When he reached maturity as a youth, in the winter cold he wrapped his feet in a quilt, placed them in a tub, and read aloud without cease.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy, during the bitter cold of winter, he would wrap his feet in a quilt, tuck them into a tub, and keep reading aloud without stopping.

sentences.zh: 中永樂二年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Yongle.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Yongle reign he qualified as a jinshi.

sentences.zh: 選庶吉士，進學文淵閣，與修《太祖實錄》。

translations.literal: He was selected as a Hanlin Bachelor and advanced to study in the Wenyuan Pavilion, joining in the compilation of the Veritable Records of Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: Selected as a Hanlin Bachelor, he entered the Wenyuan Pavilion for advanced study and took part in compiling the Veritable Records of Emperor Taizu.

sentences.zh: 授刑部主事，復與重修《實錄》。

translations.literal: He was appointed a principal secretary in the Ministry of Justice and again joined in revising the Veritable Records.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed principal secretary in the Ministry of Justice, he again participated in revising the Veritable Records.

sentences.zh: 書成，改翰林侍讀。

translations.literal: When the book was completed, he was transferred to Hanlin Reader.
translations.idiomatic: When that work was finished, he was made a Hanlin Reader.

sentences.zh: 性剛鯁，慨然以天下為己任。

translations.literal: His nature was stern and unyielding; he openly took the empire as his own responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was stern and uncompromising, and he openly treated the welfare of the realm as his personal charge.

sentences.zh: 十九年，三殿災，詔求直言。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, the three main halls burned; an edict sought forthright speech.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year of Yongle, fire destroyed the three principal palace halls, and an edict called for candid memorials.

sentences.zh: 條上時務十五事。

translations.literal: He itemized and submitted fifteen matters of contemporary affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial listing fifteen urgent matters of state.

sentences.zh: 成祖決計都北京，時方招徠遠人。

translations.literal: The Chengzu Emperor had decided to establish the capital at Beijing; at the time he was just attracting people from distant lands.
translations.idiomatic: The Yongle Emperor had already resolved to make Beijing the capital and was at that time bidding distant peoples to come.

sentences.zh: 而時勉言營建之非，及遠國入貢人不宜使群居輦下。

translations.literal: But Shimian spoke of the wrongness of construction projects, and that tribute-bearers from distant states ought not be allowed to dwell together below the imperial carriage-road.
translations.idiomatic: Shimian argued that the massive building program was ill advised, and that envoys from far countries should not be allowed to cluster together near the capital.

sentences.zh: 忤帝意。

translations.literal: He offended the emperor's wishes.
translations.idiomatic: This ran counter to the emperor's intent.

sentences.zh: 已，觀其他說，多中時病，抵之地；

translations.literal: Thereafter, when the emperor looked at his other statements, many hit the ailments of the times and were hurled to the ground;
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the emperor read his other proposals, he found many of them on target regarding contemporary abuses and flung the memorial aside in anger;

sentences.zh: 復取視者再，卒多施行。

translations.literal: he took it up to look again twice, and in the end many were put into practice.
translations.idiomatic: yet after picking it up and reading it through again, he ultimately adopted many of his recommendations.

sentences.zh: 尋被讒下獄。

translations.literal: Before long he was slandered and sent down to prison.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was denounced and imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 歲餘得釋，楊榮薦復職。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was released; Yang Rong recommended him to resume his post.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he was released, and Yang Rong recommended him for reinstatement.

sentences.zh: 宣德五年修《成祖實錄》成，遷侍讀學士。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xuande, when the compilation of the Veritable Records of Chengzu was completed, he was promoted to Reader-in-waiting of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Xuande, upon completion of the Veritable Records of the Yongle Emperor, he was promoted to Reader-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 帝幸史館，撒金錢賜諸學士。

translations.literal: The emperor visited the Historiography Institute and scattered gold coins as gifts to the academicians.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor visited the Historiography Institute, he tossed out gold coins as gifts for the academicians.

sentences.zh: 皆俯取，時勉獨正立。

translations.literal: All stooped to pick them up; only Shimian stood upright.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone else stooped to gather them, but Shimian alone remained standing upright.

sentences.zh: 帝乃出余錢賜之。

translations.literal: The emperor then brought out remaining coins and bestowed them on him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thereupon produced additional coins and had them presented to him.

sentences.zh: 正統三年以《宣宗實錄》成，進學士，掌院事兼經筵官。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhengtong, upon completion of the Veritable Records of Xuanzong, he was advanced to Academician, directing the affairs of the academy while also serving as lecturer at the Classics Colloquium.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhengtong, when the Veritable Records of the Xuande Emperor were completed, he was promoted to Hanlin Academician, put in charge of the academy, and appointed lecturer at the imperial lectures.

sentences.zh: 六年代貝泰為祭酒。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he replaced Bei Tai as Chancellor of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he succeeded Bei Tai as chancellor of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 八年乞致仕，不允。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he requested retirement; it was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he petitioned to retire, but the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 初，時勉請改建國學。

translations.literal: Earlier, Shimian had requested reconstruction of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Shimian had petitioned for rebuilding the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 帝命王振往視，時勉待振無加禮。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Wang Zhen to go inspect; Shimian received Zhen without special courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Wang Zhen to inspect the project, but Shimian treated him without any special deference.

sentences.zh: 振銜之，廉其短，無所得。

translations.literal: Zhen harbored resentment; he searched for his faults but found nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen bore a grudge and tried to uncover misconduct on his part, but found nothing.

sentences.zh: 時勉嘗芟彜倫堂樹旁枝，振遂言時勉擅伐官樹入家。

translations.literal: Shimian had once trimmed side branches from trees by the Hall of Universal Ethics; Zhen then said Shimian had arrogantly cut official trees and taken them home.
translations.idiomatic: When Shimian once pruned side branches from trees beside the Hall of Universal Ethics, Zhen accused him of unlawfully felling government trees and carrying them home.

sentences.zh: 取中旨，與司業趙琬、掌饌金鑒並枷國子監前。

translations.literal: An edict was obtained from the emperor's private command, and together with Vice-Chancellor Zhao Wan and food steward Jin Jian he was cangued before the National University.
translations.idiomatic: On the emperor's secret instruction he was shackled together with Vice-Chancellor Zhao Wan and commissary Jin Jian in front of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 官校至，時勉方坐東堂閱課士卷，徐呼諸生品第高下，顧僚屬定甲乙，揭榜乃行。

translations.literal: When the guards arrived, Shimian was just seated in the East Hall reviewing students' examination papers; he slowly called the students' ranks high and low, glanced at subordinates to fix the grades of A and B, posted the list, and only then went.
translations.idiomatic: When the arresting officers arrived, Shimian was still in the East Hall grading examination papers; unhurriedly he had the students ranked, instructed his staff to fix the marks, posted the results, and only then went with them.

sentences.zh: 方盛署，枷三日不解。

translations.literal: It was the height of summer; the cangue was not removed for three days.
translations.idiomatic: It was the height of summer, and the cangue was left on for three days without release.

sentences.zh: 監生李貴等千余人詣闕乞貸。

translations.literal: More than a thousand students such as Li Gui went to the palace gate to beg for their release on bail.
translations.idiomatic: More than a thousand students led by Li Gui went to the palace gates to plead for their release.

sentences.zh: 有石大用者，上章願以身代。

translations.literal: There was one Shi Dayong, who submitted a memorial wishing to substitute his own body.
translations.idiomatic: One student named Shi Dayong submitted a memorial offering to suffer punishment in their place.

sentences.zh: 諸生圜集朝門，呼聲徹殿庭。

translations.literal: The students gathered in a circle at the Court Gate; their cries penetrated the palace halls.
translations.idiomatic: Students crowded round the Court Gate, their shouts echoing through the palace courts.

sentences.zh: 振聞諸生不平，恐激變。

translations.literal: Zhen heard that the students were aggrieved and feared an outbreak of trouble.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhen heard of the students' outrage, he feared they might spark a riot.

sentences.zh: 及通政司奏大用章，振內慚。

translations.literal: When the Office of Transmission memorialized Dayong's document, Zhen felt inward shame.
translations.idiomatic: When the Office of Transmission forwarded Dayong's memorial, Zhen was deeply ashamed.

sentences.zh: 助教李繼請解於會昌侯孫忠。

translations.literal: Assistant Instructor Li Ji requested release through Marquis of Huichang Sun Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant instructor Li Ji sought their release through the Marquis of Huichang, Sun Zhong.

sentences.zh: 忠，皇太后父也。

translations.literal: Zhong was the empress dowager's father.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Zhong was the father of the empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 忠生日，太后使人賜忠家。

translations.literal: On Zhong's birthday the empress dowager sent people to bestow gifts on Zhong's household.
translations.idiomatic: On his birthday the empress dowager sent gifts to his home.

sentences.zh: 忠附奏太后，太后為言之帝。

translations.literal: Zhong appended a memorial to the empress dowager; the empress dowager spoke of it to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Zhong enclosed a memorial with his thanks to the empress dowager, and she spoke to the emperor on Shimian's behalf.

sentences.zh: 帝初不知也，立釋之。

translations.literal: The emperor at first did not know; he immediately released them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had not known of the matter at all and ordered their immediate release.

sentences.zh: 繼不拘檢柙，時勉嘗規切之。

translations.literal: Ji did not restrain himself within rules; Shimian had once admonished him sternly.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ji had been lax in observing discipline, and Shimian had once rebuked him sharply.

sentences.zh: 繼不能盡用，然心感時勉言，至是竟得其助。

translations.literal: Ji could not fully apply it, yet inwardly he was moved by Shimian's words; at this juncture he finally obtained his help.
translations.idiomatic: Ji had not been able to follow all his advice, yet he treasured what Shimian had said, and now repaid him by intervening.

sentences.zh: 大用，豐潤人。

translations.literal: Dayong was a native of Fengrun.
translations.idiomatic: Dayong came from Fengrun.

sentences.zh: 樸魯，初不為六館所知，及是名動京師。

translations.literal: Simple and awkward, at first he was not known among the six lodges; when this happened his name shook the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Plain and unassuming, he had barely been noticed among the six dormitory halls until this act made his name resound through the capital.

sentences.zh: 明年中鄉試，官至戶部主事。

translations.literal: The next year he passed the provincial examination; his official career reached principal secretary in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he passed the provincial examination and eventually rose to principal secretary in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 九年，帝視學。

translations.literal: In the ninth year the emperor inspected the school.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year the emperor came to inspect the university.

sentences.zh: 時勉進講《尚書》，辭旨清朗。

translations.literal: Shimian advanced to lecture on the Book of Documents; his phrasing was clear and luminous.
translations.idiomatic: Shimian lectured on the Book of Documents; his exposition was lucid and compelling.

sentences.zh: 帝悅，賜予有加。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and increased his rewards.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted and bestowed extra rewards.

sentences.zh: 連疏乞致仕，不允。

translations.literal: He sent successive memorials begging to retire; it was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly petitioned to retire, but each request was refused.

sentences.zh: 十二年春乃得請。

translations.literal: Only in the spring of the twelfth year did he obtain permission.
translations.idiomatic: Not until the spring of the twelfth year was his retirement finally granted.

sentences.zh: 朝臣及國子生餞都門外者幾三千人，或遠送至登舟，候舟發乃去。

translations.literal: Court officials and National University students who saw him off outside the capital gate numbered nearly three thousand; some escorted him far to the point of boarding the boat, waiting until the boat set out before leaving.
translations.idiomatic: Nearly three thousand court officials and university students saw him off outside the capital gate; some accompanied him all the way to his boat and did not turn back until it had cast off.

sentences.zh: 英宗北狩，時勉日夜悲慟。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yingzong went north on campaign and was taken captive, Shimian grieved day and night.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yingzong Emperor was captured on the northern campaign, Shimian mourned day and night.

sentences.zh: 遣其孫驥詣闕上書，請選將練兵，親君子，遠小人，褒表忠節，迎還車駕，復仇雪恥。

translations.literal: He sent his grandson Ji to the palace to submit a memorial, requesting selection of generals and training of troops, drawing near to gentlemen and keeping distant from petty men, commending loyalty and integrity, welcoming back the imperial carriage, and avenging the humiliation.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his grandson Ji to court with a memorial urging the selection of able generals, training of troops, favor toward worthy men and distance from flatterers, honors for the loyal, recovery of the captive emperor, and revenge for the national disgrace.

sentences.zh: 景泰元年得旨褒答，而時勉卒矣，年七十七。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingtai he received an edict of commendation in reply, but Shimian had already died, aged seventy-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jingtai the court issued a commendatory reply, but by then Shimian had died at the age of seventy-seven.

sentences.zh: 謚文毅。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Wenyi.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted the posthumous title Wenyi, meaning Cultivated and Resolute.

sentences.zh: 成化五年，以其孫颙請，改謚忠文，贈禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Chenghua, on his grandson Yong's petition, the title was changed to Zhongwen, and he was posthumously made Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Chenghua, at the request of his grandson Yong, his posthumous title was changed to Zhongwen, meaning Loyal and Literary, and he was posthumously appointed vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 時勉為祭酒六年，列格、致、誠、正四號，訓勵甚切。

translations.literal: Shimian served as Chancellor for six years; he established four mottos—Ge, Zhi, Cheng, and Zheng—and admonished with great urgency.
translations.idiomatic: During his six years as chancellor he instituted the four mottos Discipline, Diligence, Integrity, and Rectitude, enforcing them with exceptional rigor.

sentences.zh: 崇廉恥，抑奔競，別賢否，示勸懲。

translations.literal: He honored integrity and shame, suppressed frantic competition, distinguished worthy from unworthy, and displayed encouragement and punishment.
translations.idiomatic: He upheld integrity, curbed unseemly rivalry, distinguished the worthy from the unworthy, and made clear what conduct would be rewarded or punished.

sentences.zh: 諸生貧不能婚葬者，節省餐錢為贍給。

translations.literal: For students too poor to marry or bury kin, he economized meal funds to provide support.
translations.idiomatic: Students too poor to marry or bury relatives were helped from funds he saved by cutting back on their meal allowances.

sentences.zh: 督令讀書，燈火達旦，吟誦聲不絕，人才盛於昔時。

translations.literal: He supervised and ordered study; lamps burned until dawn and chanting voices never ceased; talent flourished beyond former times.
translations.idiomatic: He drove them to study until lamps burned all night and recitation never ceased, and the quality of graduates surpassed any earlier age.

sentences.zh: 始，太祖以宋訥為祭酒，最有名。

translations.literal: At the beginning, Taizu took Song Na as Chancellor; he was most famous.
translations.idiomatic: Under the founding emperor, Song Na had served as chancellor and enjoyed the greatest renown.

sentences.zh: 其後寧化張顯宗申明學規，人比之訥。

translations.literal: Afterward Zhang Xianzong of Ninghua clarified the study regulations; people compared him to Na.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhang Xianzong of Ninghua reformed the regulations and was compared to Song Na.

sentences.zh: 而胡儼當成祖之世，尤稱人師。

translations.literal: Yet Hu Yan in the age of Chengzu was especially acclaimed as a teacher of men.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Yan in the Yongle reign was especially celebrated as a teacher.

sentences.zh: 然以直節重望為士類所依歸者，莫如時勉。

translations.literal: Yet among those whom scholar-officials relied on for integrity and weighty reputation, none matched Shimian.
translations.idiomatic: Yet for integrity and moral authority on which scholars relied, none compared to Shimian.

sentences.zh: 英國公張輔暨諸侯伯奏，願偕詣國子監聽講。

translations.literal: Grand Preceptor of the State Zhang Fu together with marquises and earls memorialized, wishing together to go to the National University to listen to lectures.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Ying, Zhang Fu, and other nobles memorialized asking to attend lectures together at the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 帝命以三月三日往。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered them to go on the third day of the third month.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor directed them to come on the third day of the third month.

sentences.zh: 時勉升師席，諸生以次立，講《五經》各一章。

translations.literal: Shimian ascended the teacher's seat; students stood in order; he lectured on one chapter each from the Five Classics.
translations.idiomatic: Shimian took the master's seat while the students stood in ranks; he lectured on one chapter from each of the Five Classics.

sentences.zh: 畢事，設酒饌，諸侯伯讓曰：「受教之地，當就諸生列坐。」

translations.literal: When the affair was finished, wine and food were set out; the marquises and earls yielded, saying: "This is a place for receiving instruction; we ought to take seats among the students' rows.
translations.idiomatic: When the lectures ended, a feast was laid out. The nobles insisted: "This is where we have come to be taught; we should sit in the students' ranks.

sentences.zh: 惟輔與抗禮。

translations.literal: Only Fu treated him as an equal in ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Only Zhang Fu treated him as an equal in rank.

sentences.zh: 諸生歌《鹿鳴》之詩，賓主雍雍，盡暮散去，人稱為太平盛事。

translations.literal: The students sang the poem "Luming"; host and guests were harmonious; they dispersed only at evening's end; people called it a flourishing age's grand occasion.
translations.idiomatic: The students sang the "Luming" ode; host and guests mingled in perfect harmony until dusk, and contemporaries hailed it as a scene befitting a golden age of peace.

sentences.zh: 陳敬宗，字光世，慈溪人。

translations.literal: Chen Jingzong, style name Guangshi, was a native of Cixi.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jingzong, whose style name was Guangshi, came from Cixi.

sentences.zh: 永樂二年進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi of the second year of Yongle.
translations.idiomatic: He qualified as a jinshi in the second year of Yongle.

sentences.zh: 選庶吉士，進學文淵閣，與修《永樂大典》。

translations.literal: Selected as Hanlin Bachelor, he advanced to study in Wenyuan Pavilion and joined in compiling the Yongle Encyclopedia.
translations.idiomatic: Selected as a Hanlin Bachelor, he studied in the Wenyuan Pavilion and helped compile the Yongle Encyclopedia.

sentences.zh: 書成，授刑部主事。

translations.literal: When the book was completed, he was appointed principal secretary in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: When that work was finished he was appointed principal secretary in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 又與修《五經四書大全》，再修《太祖實錄》，授翰林侍講。

translations.literal: He again joined in compiling the Great Compendium of the Five Classics and Four Books, revised again the Veritable Records of Taizu, and was appointed Hanlin Lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: He also worked on the Great Compendium of the Five Classics and Four Books, again revised the Veritable Records of Taizu, and was made a Hanlin Lecturer.

sentences.zh: 內艱歸。

translations.literal: He returned home on bereavement for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He returned home to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 宣德元年起修兩朝實錄。

translations.literal: From the first year of Xuande he began compiling the veritable records of the two reigns.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xuande he began work on the veritable records of the two preceding reigns.

sentences.zh: 明年轉南京國子監司業。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to be Vice-Chancellor of the Nanjing National University.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was transferred to vice chancellor of the Nanjing Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 帝諭之曰：「侍講，清華之選；

translations.literal: The emperor instructed him, saying: "Reader is a choice of pure brilliance;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told him: "A Hanlin lecturer is chosen from the most brilliant scholars;

sentences.zh: 司業，師儒之席。

translations.literal: Vice-Chancellor is the seat of the teacher and scholar.
translations.idiomatic: a vice chancellor holds the chair of a master teacher.

sentences.zh: 位雖不崇，任則重矣。」

translations.literal: The rank is not lofty, but the responsibility is weighty.
translations.idiomatic: The post is not exalted in rank, but the burden is heavy.

sentences.zh: 九年，秩滿，選祭酒，正統三年上書言：「舊制，諸生以在監久近，送諸司歷事。

translations.literal: In the ninth year his term was complete and he was selected as Chancellor; in the third year of Zhengtong he submitted a memorial stating: "By the old system, students according to how long they had been in the directorate were sent to various offices for practical service.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year his term expired and he was appointed chancellor. In the third year of Zhengtong he memorialized: "Under the old rules, students were posted to government offices for practical training according to how long they had studied at the university.

sentences.zh: 比來，有因事予告者，遷延累歲，至撥送之期始赴，實長奸惰，請以肄業多寡為次第。

translations.literal: Recently, some who took leave for affairs delayed year after year, and only at the time of assignment went; this truly fosters deceit and laziness. Please take advancement in studies as the order of precedence.
translations.idiomatic: Lately some who secured leave dragged on for years and only showed up when their turn came, which only encourages sloth and evasion. I ask that order of assignment be based on progress in one's studies.

sentences.zh: 又近有願就雜職之例，士風卑陋，誠非細故，請加禁止。」

translations.literal: Moreover recently there has been the precedent of wishing to take miscellaneous posts; scholarly custom is base and mean—this is truly no small matter; please add prohibition.
translations.idiomatic: There is also a recent trend of students volunteering for low clerical posts, which debases scholarly standards. This is no trifle; I ask that it be forbidden.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: It was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved both proposals.

sentences.zh: 敬宗美須髯，容儀端整，步履有定則，力以師道自任。

translations.literal: Jingzong had handsome beard and whiskers, bearing dignified and orderly, steps with fixed rule; he strove to take the teacher's Way as his own charge.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong had a fine beard and dignified bearing; he walked with measured steps and held himself wholly accountable as a master teacher.

sentences.zh: 立教條，革陋習。

translations.literal: He established teaching regulations and reformed vulgar habits.
translations.idiomatic: He set down rules of instruction and swept away corrupt practices.

sentences.zh: 六館士千余人，每升堂聽講，設饌會食，整肅如朝廷。

translations.literal: More than a thousand students in the six lodges, each time they ascended the hall to hear lectures, set out food and dined together, as orderly as at court.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever more than a thousand students of the six halls assembled for lectures, their shared meals were conducted with the decorum of a court audience.

sentences.zh: 稍失容，即令待罪堂下。

translations.literal: If they were slightly out of decorum, he immediately ordered them to await punishment below the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who lapsed even slightly in deportment was made to stand in penance below the lecture hall.

sentences.zh: 僚屬憚其嚴，誣以他事，訟之法司。

translations.literal: His subordinates feared his severity and slandered him on other matters, taking the case to the judicial offices.
translations.idiomatic: Staff who feared his strictness trumped up charges and brought him before the judiciary.

sentences.zh: 周忱與敬宗善，曰：「盍具疏自理。」

translations.literal: Zhou Chen was on good terms with Jingzong and said: "Why not prepare a memorial to explain yourself?
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Chen, who was friendly with him, urged: "Why not submit a memorial in your own defense?

sentences.zh: 為屬草，辭稍遷就。

translations.literal: He drafted one for him; the wording was somewhat accommodating.
translations.idiomatic: Chen drafted a text for him, but the language was unduly conciliatory.

sentences.zh: 敬宗驚曰：「得無誑君耶？」

translations.literal: Jingzong said in alarm: "Surely this is not deceiving the sovereign?
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong exclaimed: "Would this not amount to deceiving the emperor?

sentences.zh: 不果上，事亦竟白。

translations.literal: In the end it was not submitted, and the matter was finally cleared.
translations.idiomatic: He never filed it, and the affair was eventually resolved in his favor.

sentences.zh: 滿考，入京師，王振欲見之，令忱道意。

translations.literal: When his term was complete he entered the capital; Wang Zhen wished to see him and had Chen convey his intent.
translations.idiomatic: After his term ended he went to Beijing; the eunuch Wang Zhen wanted an audience and asked Zhou Chen to convey the invitation.

sentences.zh: 敬宗曰：「吾為諸生師表，而私謁中貴，何以對諸生？」

translations.literal: Jingzong said: "I am the model teacher for the students—how can I pay a private visit to a palace favorite? How would I face the students?
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong replied: "I am these students' moral exemplar. How could I pay a private call on a court eunuch? What account could I give my pupils?

sentences.zh: 振知不可屈，乃貽之文錦羊酒，求書程子《四箴》，冀其來謝。

translations.literal: Zhen knew he could not be bent and therefore sent him patterned brocade, mutton, and wine, requesting a copy of Master Cheng's Four Admonitions, hoping he would come to give thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing he could not be swayed, Zhen sent brocade, mutton, and wine, asking him to write out Master Cheng's Four Admonitions in the hope he would come to offer thanks.

sentences.zh: 敬宗書訖，署名而已。

translations.literal: When Jingzong had finished writing, he signed his name and nothing more.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong wrote out the text, signed his name, and sent it back.

sentences.zh: 返其幣，終不往見。

translations.literal: He returned the gifts and never went to see him.
translations.idiomatic: He returned the gifts and never called on Zhen.

sentences.zh: 王直為吏部尚書，從容謂曰：「先生官司成久，將薦公為司寇。」

translations.literal: Wang Zhi was Minister of Personnel and said to him at leisure: "Sir, you have held office long; I intend to recommend you as Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Personnel Wang Zhi said to him gently: "You have served here many years; I mean to recommend you for Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 敬宗曰：「公知我者，今與天下英才終日論議，顧不樂耶？」

translations.literal: Jingzong said: "You know me—now I debate all day with the empire's finest talents. Would I not be happy?"
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong answered: "You know my mind. Debating all day with the realm's best scholars—what office could be more satisfying?"

sentences.zh: 性善飲酒，至數鬥不亂。

translations.literal: By nature he was fond of wine and could drink several dou without disorder.
translations.idiomatic: He loved wine and could drink several dou without losing his composure.

sentences.zh: 襄城伯李隆守備南京，每留飲，聲伎滿左右。

translations.literal: Li Long, Earl of Xiangcheng, garrisoned Nanjing and often kept him for drinking; musicians and dancers filled the room on either side.
translations.idiomatic: The Earl of Xiangcheng, Li Long, who defended Nanjing, often entertained him with wine while musicians and dancers thronged the hall.

sentences.zh: 竟日舉杯，未嘗一盼。

translations.literal: All day he raised his cup and never once glanced at them.
translations.idiomatic: He drank through the day without once glancing at the performers.

sentences.zh: 其嚴重如此。

translations.literal: His gravity was like this.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the weight of his bearing.

sentences.zh: 十二年冬乞休，不允。

translations.literal: In the winter of the twelfth year he begged to retire; it was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he petitioned to retire in winter, but was refused.

sentences.zh: 景泰元年九月與尚書魏驥同引年致仕。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the first year of Jingtai he cited age together with Minister Wei Ji to retire.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the first year of Jingtai he retired on grounds of age together with Wei Ji, minister of works.

sentences.zh: 家居不輕出。

translations.literal: At home he did not go out lightly.
translations.idiomatic: In retirement he rarely left his house.

sentences.zh: 有被其容接者，莫不興起。

translations.literal: Those who received his company were all stirred to improvement.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever was granted his company came away inspired.

sentences.zh: 天順三年五月卒，年八十三。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the third year of Tianshun he died, aged eighty-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifth month of the third year of Tianshun at the age of eighty-three.

sentences.zh: 後贈禮部侍郎，謚文定。

translations.literal: Later he was posthumously made Vice Minister of Rites with the posthumous title Wendiing.
translations.idiomatic: He was later posthumously appointed vice minister of rites with the title Wendiing, meaning Settled in Culture.

sentences.zh: 初，敬宗與李時勉同在翰林，袁忠徹嘗相之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Jingzong and Li Shimian were together in the Hanlin; Yuan Zhongche once read their physiognomy.
translations.idiomatic: Early on Jingzong and Li Shimian had served together in the Hanlin; Yuan Zhongche once examined their faces.

sentences.zh: 曳二人並列曰：「二公他日功名相埒。」

translations.literal: He drew the two men to stand side by side and said: "These two lords' future fame and rank will be equal.
translations.idiomatic: Pulling them to stand together he said: "These two gentlemen will one day attain equal eminence.

sentences.zh: 敬宗儀觀魁梧，時勉貌稍寢，後二人同時為兩京祭酒。

translations.literal: Jingzong's bearing was tall and imposing; Shimian's looks were somewhat plain; later the two at the same time became chancellors of the two capitals' universities.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong was tall and striking in appearance, Shimian somewhat plain of face; yet both later served simultaneously as chancellors of the Nanjing and Beijing universities.

sentences.zh: 時勉平恕得士，敬宗方嚴。

translations.literal: Shimian was lenient and won over the scholars; Jingzong was strict.
translations.idiomatic: Shimian was easygoing and won students' hearts; Jingzong was severe.

sentences.zh: 終明世稱賢祭酒者，曰南陳北李。

translations.literal: Throughout the Ming, those called worthy chancellors were spoken of as "Chen in the south, Li in the north."
translations.idiomatic: For the whole Ming period the pair were remembered as the worthy chancellors of the south and north—Chen and Li.

sentences.zh: 劉鉉，字宗器，長洲人。

translations.literal: Liu Xuan, style name Zongqi, was a native of Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xuan, whose style name was Zongqi, came from Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 生彌月而孤。

translations.literal: He was orphaned a month after birth.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his father when only a month old.

sentences.zh: 及長，刲股療母疾。

translations.literal: When grown, he cut flesh from his thigh to treat his mother's illness.
translations.idiomatic: As an adult he cut flesh from his thigh to treat his mother's illness.

sentences.zh: 母卒，哀毀，以孝聞。

translations.literal: When his mother died he mourned with devastation and became known for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: When she died he mourned with such devastation that his filial piety became renowned.

sentences.zh: 永樂中，用善書征入翰林，舉順天鄉試，授中書舍人。

translations.literal: In the Yongle period, because of skill in calligraphy he was summoned into the Hanlin, passed the Shuntian provincial examination, and was appointed Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongle his fine calligraphy brought him into the Hanlin; he passed the Shuntian provincial examination and was made a secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 宣德時，預修成祖、仁宗《實錄》，遷兵部主事，仍供事內廷。

translations.literal: In the Xuande period he took part in compiling the veritable records of Chengzu and Renzong, was transferred to principal secretary in the Ministry of War, and still served in the inner court.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xuande he helped compile the veritable records of the Yongle and Hongxi emperors, rose to principal secretary in the Ministry of War, and continued serving in the inner court.

sentences.zh: 正統中，再修《宣宗實錄》，進侍講。

translations.literal: In the Zhengtong period he again revised the Veritable Records of Xuanzong and was advanced to Lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhengtong reign he again revised the Veritable Records of the Xuande Emperor and was promoted to lecturer.

sentences.zh: 以學士曹鼐等薦，與修撰王振教習庶吉士。

translations.literal: On the recommendation of Academician Cao Nai and others, together with Reviser Wang Zhen he instructed the Hanlin Bachelors.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended by Academician Cao Nai and others, he joined Reviser Wang Zhen in instructing the Hanlin Bachelors.

sentences.zh: 景帝立，進侍講學士，直經筵。

translations.literal: When the Jingdi Emperor ascended, he was advanced to Lecturer-in-waiting and attended the Classics Colloquium.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Jingdi took the throne he was made lecturer-in-waiting and attended the imperial lectures.

sentences.zh: 三年，以高谷薦，遷國子祭酒。

translations.literal: In the third year, on Gao Gu's recommendation, he was transferred to Chancellor of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, on Gao Gu's recommendation, he was appointed chancellor of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 時以國計不足，放遣諸生，不願歸者停其月廩。

translations.literal: At the time because state finances were insufficient, students were sent away; those unwilling to return had their monthly stipends stopped.
translations.idiomatic: State finances were tight and students were sent home; those who refused to leave had their monthly stipends cut off.

sentences.zh: 鉉言：「養才，國家急務。

translations.literal: Xuan said: "Nurturing talent is an urgent task of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan memorialized: "Cultivating talent is among the state's most urgent duties.

sentences.zh: 今倉廩尚盈，奈何靳此？」

translations.literal: The granaries are still full—why be stingy with this?
translations.idiomatic: Our granaries are still stocked—why withhold these allowances?

sentences.zh: 遂得復給。

translations.literal: The stipends were thereupon restored.
translations.idiomatic: The stipends were restored.

sentences.zh: 又今甄別六館生，年老貌寢，學藝疏淺者，斥為民。

translations.literal: Moreover, at that time the six lodges' students were being screened; those old in years, plain in looks, and shallow in learning were expelled as commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Students in the six halls were also being culled; the elderly, homely, and academically weak were dismissed as commoners.

sentences.zh: 鉉言：「諸生荷教澤久，豈無片長？

translations.literal: Xuan said: "The students have long received our teaching—can they have no merit at all?
translations.idiomatic: Xuan argued: "These men have long enjoyed our instruction—surely each has some strength?

sentences.zh: 況離親戚，棄墳墓，艱苦備至，一旦被斥，非朝廷育才意。

translations.literal: Moreover they have left kin and abandoned ancestral graves, suffering every hardship; once expelled, this is not the court's intent in nurturing talent.
translations.idiomatic: They have left families and ancestral graves and endured every hardship; to cast them out betrays the court's purpose in educating them.

sentences.zh: 乞揀年貌衰而有學者，量授之官。」

translations.literal: I beg to select those advanced in years but still learned and grant them offices in due measure.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that those who are older yet still learned be given appropriate posts.

sentences.zh: 帝可其奏。

translations.literal: The emperor approved his memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his proposal.

sentences.zh: 尋以母喪歸。

translations.literal: Before long he returned home on his mother's death.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he went home to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 服闕，赴都，陳詢已為祭酒。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he went to the capital; Chen Xun was already chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he returned to the capital, where Chen Xun already held the chancellorship.

sentences.zh: 帝重鉉，命與詢並任。

translations.literal: The emperor valued Xuan and ordered him to serve together with Xun.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor esteemed Xuan and appointed him to serve alongside Xun.

sentences.zh: 天順初，改少詹事，侍東宮講讀。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianshun he was made Junior Mentor and attended the Eastern Palace lectures.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianshun he became junior mentor and lectured the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 明年十月卒。

translations.literal: The next year in the tenth month he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died the following tenth month.

sentences.zh: 帝及太子皆賜祭，賻贈有加。

translations.literal: The emperor and crown prince both bestowed sacrifices; funeral gifts were increased.
translations.idiomatic: Both emperor and crown prince sent sacrificial offerings and enriched funeral gifts.

sentences.zh: 憲宗立，贈禮部侍郎，謚文恭。

translations.literal: When the Xianzong Emperor ascended, he was posthumously made Vice Minister of Rites with the title Wengong.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xianzong took the throne he was posthumously made vice minister of rites with the title Wengong, meaning Reverent and Respectful.

sentences.zh: 鉉性介特，言行不茍。

translations.literal: Xuan's nature was upright and peculiar; in word and deed he was not lax.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan was upright and uncompromising, exacting in speech and conduct.

sentences.zh: 教庶吉士及課國子生，規條嚴整，讀書至老彌篤。

translations.literal: In teaching Hanlin Bachelors and examining National University students, his regulations were strict and orderly; he read books with growing devotion even into old age.
translations.idiomatic: Whether instructing Hanlin Bachelors or examining university students, his rules were rigorous, and he read with deepening devotion into old age.

sentences.zh: 仲子瀚以進士使南方。

translations.literal: His second son Han went south as an envoy after qualifying as jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Han, a jinshi, was sent on a mission to the south.

sentences.zh: 瀕行，閱其衣篋。

translations.literal: Before he left, Xuan inspected his clothing chest.
translations.idiomatic: Before Han departed, Xuan inspected his luggage.

sentences.zh: 比還，篋如故，乃喜曰：「無玷吾門矣。」

translations.literal: When he returned the chest was as before; Xuan rejoiced and said: "You have not stained our house.
translations.idiomatic: On his return the chest was unchanged, and Xuan said with delight: "You have not dishonored our family.

sentences.zh: 瀚官終副使，能守父訓。

translations.literal: Han's highest office was vice commissioner and he was able to keep his father's instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Han rose to vice commissioner and lived by his father's teaching.

sentences.zh: 薩琦，字廷珪。

translations.literal: Sa Qi, style name Tinggui.
translations.idiomatic: Sa Qi, whose style name was Tinggui.

sentences.zh: 其先西域人，後著籍閩縣。

translations.literal: His ancestors were Western Region people; later they were registered in Min County.
translations.idiomatic: His family came from the Western Regions and was later registered in Min County, Fujian.

sentences.zh: 舉宣德五年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the fifth year of Xuande.
translations.idiomatic: He qualified as jinshi in the fifth year of Xuande.

sentences.zh: 歷官禮部侍郎兼少詹事。

translations.literal: He served as Vice Minister of Rites while also holding Junior Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: He served as vice minister of rites and junior mentor.

sentences.zh: 天順元年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the first year of Tianshun.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of Tianshun.

sentences.zh: 琦有文德，狷潔不茍合。

translations.literal: Qi had literary virtue and was fastidious and upright, unwilling to compromise.
translations.idiomatic: Qi was learned and upright, unwilling to compromise his principles.

sentences.zh: 名行與鉉相頡頏云。

translations.literal: In fame and conduct he matched Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: His reputation rivaled Liu Xuan's.

sentences.zh: 邢讓，字遜之。

translations.literal: Xing Rang, style name Xunzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Xing Rang, whose style name was Xunzhi.

sentences.zh: 襄陵人。

translations.literal: A native of Xiangling.
translations.idiomatic: He came from Xiangling.

sentences.zh: 年十八，舉於鄉，入國子監。

translations.literal: At eighteen he passed the provincial examination and entered the National University.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen he passed the provincial examination and entered the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 為李時勉所器，與劉珝齊名。

translations.literal: He was prized by Li Shimian and was as famous as Liu Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shimian singled him out for praise; he was ranked with Liu Yu.

sentences.zh: 登正統十三年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the thirteenth year of Zhengtong.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in the thirteenth year of Zhengtong.

sentences.zh: 改庶吉士，授檢討。

translations.literal: He was made a Hanlin Bachelor and appointed Reviser.
translations.idiomatic: He was selected as a Hanlin Bachelor and appointed reviser.

sentences.zh: 景泰元年，李實自瓦剌還，請再遣使迎上皇。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingtai, Li Shi returned from the Oirats and requested that envoys again be sent to welcome the former emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jingtai, Li Shi returned from the Oirats and urged another embassy to bring back the captive emperor.

sentences.zh: 景帝不許。

translations.literal: The Jingdi Emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jingdi refused.

sentences.zh: 讓疏曰：「上皇於陛下有君之義，有兄之恩，安得而不迎？

translations.literal: Rang memorialized: "The former emperor toward Your Majesty has the righteousness of sovereign and the kindness of elder brother—how can he not be welcomed?
translations.idiomatic: Rang submitted: "Toward Your Majesty the former emperor bears both the bond of sovereign and the kindness of an elder brother—how can we fail to welcome him home?

sentences.zh: 且令寇假大義以問我，其何辭以應？

translations.literal: Moreover, if we let the enemy borrow righteousness to question us, what words could we answer with?
translations.idiomatic: If the enemy invokes righteousness to press us, what answer could we give?

sentences.zh: 若從群臣請，仍命實賫敕以往，且述迎復之指。

translations.literal: If we follow the ministers' request and again order Shi to carry an edict thither, stating also the intent to welcome and restore him,
translations.idiomatic: If we follow the court and again send Shi with an imperial edict explaining our intent to restore him,

sentences.zh: 雖上皇還否未可必，而陛下恩義之篤昭然於天下。

translations.literal: although whether the former emperor returns cannot yet be known, Your Majesty's depth of kindness and righteousness will shine before the empire.
translations.idiomatic: whether he actually returns remains uncertain, yet Your Majesty's devotion to kin and duty will be plain to all under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 萬一迎而不許，則我得責直於彼，以興問罪之師，不亦善乎。」

translations.literal: If in the end we welcome him but are not permitted to return, then we can hold them at fault and raise an army to demand justice—is this not also good?
translations.idiomatic: If we welcome him and are refused, we can blame them and march to punish the wrong—would that not also be wise?

sentences.zh: 疏入，帝委曲諭解之。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, the emperor tactfully explained and pacified him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor received the memorial and gently reasoned with him.

sentences.zh: 天順末，父憂歸。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianshun he returned home on his father's death.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Tianshun he went home to mourn his father.

sentences.zh: 未終喪，起修《英宗實錄》，進修撰。

translations.literal: Before mourning ended he was recalled to compile the Veritable Records of Yingzong and was advanced to Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: Before mourning ended he was recalled to compile the Veritable Records of the Yingzong Emperor and promoted to compiler.

sentences.zh: 成化二年超遷國子祭酒。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chenghua he was promoted over the usual steps to Chancellor of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Chenghua he was unusually promoted straight to university chancellor.

sentences.zh: 慈懿太后崩，議祔廟禮，讓率僚屬疏諫。

translations.literal: When the Empress Dowager Ciyi died, the rites for enshrining her in the ancestral temple were debated; Rang led his staff in memorial protest.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Ciyi died, Rang led his colleagues in protesting plans to enshrine her in the imperial ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 兩京國學教官，例不得遷擢，讓等以為言，由科目者，滿考得銓敘。

translations.literal: Instructors in the two capitals' universities by precedent could not be transferred or promoted; Rang and others spoke on this, and those from the examination track, when their terms were complete, could be evaluated and appointed.
translations.idiomatic: University instructors in both capitals could not normally be promoted; Rang secured evaluations and appointments for those who had served out their terms.

sentences.zh: 讓在太學，亦力以師道自任，修《辟雍通志》，督諸生誦小學及諸經。

translations.literal: Rang at the Imperial Academy also strove to take the teacher's Way as his charge, compiled the Comprehensive Gazetteer of the Imperial Academy, and supervised students in reciting the Elementary Learning and the classics.
translations.idiomatic: As chancellor he compiled the Comprehensive Gazetteer of the Imperial Academy and required students to recite the Elementary Learning and the classics.

sentences.zh: 痛懲謁告之弊，時以此見稱，而謗者亦眾。

translations.literal: He punished harshly the abuse of leave petitions; for this he was praised at the time, but there were also many who slandered him.
translations.idiomatic: He cracked down on abuses of leave, winning praise but also many enemies.

sentences.zh: 為人負才狹中。

translations.literal: As a man he was talented but narrow-minded.
translations.idiomatic: He was gifted but petty.

sentences.zh: 意所輕重，輒形於詞色，名位相軋者多忌之。

translations.literal: Whomever he favored or disfavored showed at once in his words and face; many of those he rivaled in rank and fame envied him.
translations.idiomatic: His likes and dislikes showed plainly in speech and expression, and many peers envied him.

sentences.zh: 五年擢禮部右侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was promoted to Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was made vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 越二年，以在國子監用會饌錢事，與後祭酒陳鑒、司業張業、典籍王允等，俱得罪坐死。

translations.literal: Two years later, on the matter of using communal feast funds while chancellor of the National University, together with his successor Chancellor Chen Jian, Vice-Chancellor Zhang Ye, Archivist Wang Yun, and others, he was all found guilty and sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he and Chen Jian, Zhang Ye, Wang Yun, and others were condemned to death over misuse of communal feast funds at the university.

sentences.zh: 諸生訴闕下，請代。

translations.literal: Students appealed at the palace gate, asking to substitute themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Students petitioned at the palace gates offering to die in their place.

sentences.zh: 復詔廷臣雜治，卒坐死，贖為民。

translations.literal: An edict again ordered court officials to try the case jointly; in the end they were condemned to death but ransomed and reduced to commoners.
translations.idiomatic: The case was retried by the court; they were again sentenced to death but commuted to commoner status after ransom.

sentences.zh: 鑒既得罪，吏部尚書姚夔請起致仕禮部侍郎李紹為祭酒。

translations.literal: After Jian was punished, Minister of Personnel Yao Kui requested to recall the retired Vice Minister of Rites Li Shao as chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: After Chen Jian's fall, Yao Kui asked to recall the retired Li Shao as chancellor.

sentences.zh: 馳召之，而紹已卒。

translations.literal: They hurried to summon him, but Shao had already died.
translations.idiomatic: An urgent summons went out, but Shao was already dead.

sentences.zh: 紹字克述，安福人。

translations.literal: Shao, style name Keshu, was a native of Anfu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shao, style name Keshu, came from Anfu.

sentences.zh: 宣德八年進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the eighth year of Xuande.
translations.idiomatic: He qualified as jinshi in the eighth year of Xuande.

sentences.zh: 改庶吉士，授檢討。

translations.literal: He was made a Hanlin Bachelor and appointed Reviser.
translations.idiomatic: He became a Hanlin Bachelor and reviser.

sentences.zh: 大學士楊士奇臥病，英宗遣使詢人才，士奇舉紹等五人以對。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Yang Shiqi lay ill; the Yingzong Emperor sent an envoy to ask about talent, and Shiqi named Shao and four others in reply.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Secretary Yang Shiqi fell ill, the Yingzong Emperor asked whom to employ; Shiqi recommended Shao and four others.

sentences.zh: 土木之敗，京師戒嚴，朝士多遣家南徙。

translations.literal: At the disaster of Tumu, the capital was placed under martial law; many court officials sent their families south.
translations.idiomatic: After the Tumu disaster Beijing was placed under martial law, and many officials sent their families south.

sentences.zh: 紹曰：「主辱臣死，奚以家為？」

translations.literal: Shao said: "When the sovereign is shamed the minister must die—what use is one's household?
translations.idiomatic: Shao said: "When the ruler is disgraced, a minister should die for it—what does family matter?

sentences.zh: 卒不遣。

translations.literal: In the end he did not send them away.
translations.idiomatic: He never sent his family away.

sentences.zh: 累遷翰林學士。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 以李賢、王翺薦，擢禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: On the recommendation of Li Xian and Wang Ao he was promoted to Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xian and Wang Ao recommended him, and he was made vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 成化二年以疾求解職。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chenghua he begged to leave office on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Chenghua he resigned because of illness.

sentences.zh: 紹好學問，居官剛正有器局，能獎掖後進。

translations.literal: Shao loved learning; in office he was upright and had breadth of vision, able to encourage and lift up juniors.
translations.idiomatic: He was learned, upright, and broad-minded in office, and mentored younger officials.

sentences.zh: 其卒也，帝深惜之。

translations.literal: At his death the emperor deeply regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor deeply mourned his death.

sentences.zh: 林瀚，字亨大，閩人。

translations.literal: Lin Han, style name Hengda, was a native of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Han, whose style name was Hengda, came from Fujian.

sentences.zh: 父元美，永樂末進士，撫州知府。

translations.literal: His father Yuanmei was a jinshi at the end of Yongle and served as prefect of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yuanmei qualified as jinshi late in Yongle and became prefect of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 瀚舉成化二年進士。

translations.literal: Han passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Chenghua.
translations.idiomatic: Han became a jinshi in the second year of Chenghua.

sentences.zh: 改庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: He was made a Hanlin Bachelor and appointed Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He was selected as a Hanlin Bachelor and appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 再遷諭德，請急歸。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Preceptor and requested urgent leave to return home.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to preceptor, he asked for emergency leave to return home.

sentences.zh: 弘治初，召修《憲宗實錄》。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Hongzhi he was summoned to compile the Veritable Records of Xianzong.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Hongzhi he was recalled to compile the Veritable Records of the Xianzong Emperor.

sentences.zh: 充經筵講官。

translations.literal: He served as lecturer at the Classics Colloquium.
translations.idiomatic: He lectured at the imperial Classics Colloquium.

sentences.zh: 稍遷國子監祭酒，進禮部右侍郎，掌監事如故。

translations.literal: He was gradually transferred to Chancellor of the National University, advanced to Vice Minister of Rites, and directed the directorate as before.
translations.idiomatic: He became university chancellor, then vice minister of rites, while continuing to direct the academy.

sentences.zh: 典國學垂十年，饌銀歲以百數計，悉貯之官，以次營立署舍。

translations.literal: He directed the Imperial Academy for nearly ten years; meal funds amounting to hundreds each year were all stored in the office and used in turn to build official residences.
translations.idiomatic: For nearly ten years as chancellor he banked hundreds of taels of annual meal funds in the office treasury and used them to build staff housing.

sentences.zh: 師儒免僦居，由瀚始。

translations.literal: Teachers and scholars freed from renting lodgings began with Han.
translations.idiomatic: University teachers were first freed from renting quarters under his tenure.

sentences.zh: 歷吏部左、右侍郎。

translations.literal: He served as Left and Right Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He served as left and right vice minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 十三年拜南京吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was appointed Minister of Personnel in Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was made minister of personnel in Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 以災異率群僚陳十二事。

translations.literal: Because of calamities and anomalies he led the officials in presenting twelve matters.
translations.idiomatic: Responding to omens and disasters, he led his colleagues in memorializing on twelve issues.

sentences.zh: 御史王獻臣自遼東逮下詔獄，儒士孫伯堅等夤緣為中書舍人。

translations.literal: Censor Wang Xianchen was arrested from Liaodong and sent to the imperial prison; scholar Sun Bojian and others used connections to become Secretariat Drafters.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Wang Xianchen was jailed after returning from Liaodong, while scholars such as Sun Bojian bought their way into secretariat posts.

sentences.zh: 瀚疏爭，忤旨。

translations.literal: Han memorialized in protest and offended the imperial will.
translations.idiomatic: Han protested by memorial and offended the throne.

sentences.zh: 乞罷，不許。

translations.literal: He begged to resign; it was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to resign but was refused.

sentences.zh: 已，奏請重根本：曰保固南京，曰佑啟皇儲，曰撫綏百姓，曰增進賢才。

translations.literal: Thereafter he memorialized on strengthening the foundations: securing Nanjing, protecting and nurturing the heir, comforting the people, and advancing worthy talent.
translations.idiomatic: He then urged strengthening the dynasty's foundations: securing Nanjing, safeguarding the heir, caring for the people, and promoting talent.

sentences.zh: 瀚素剛方，與守備中官不合，他內臣進貢道其地者，瀚每裁抑之，遂交譖於劉瑾。

translations.literal: Han had always been stern and square; he did not get along with the defending eunuch, and when other inner eunuchs passed through on tribute missions he often restrained them, so they together slandered him to Liu Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Upright and unyielding, he clashed with the garrison eunuch and curbed tribute missions; the eunuchs denounced him to Liu Jin.

sentences.zh: 會劉健、謝遷罷政，瀚聞太息。

translations.literal: When Liu Jian and Xie Qian left office, Han heard and sighed deeply.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Jian and Xie Qian were dismissed, Han sighed in dismay.

sentences.zh: 言官戴銑等以留健、遷被征，瀚獨贐送，瑾聞益恨。

translations.literal: Censor Dai Xian and others were summoned because they had urged keeping Jian and Qian; Han alone sent them parting gifts; when Jin heard he hated him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: When censor Dai Xian was punished for defending Liu Jian and Xie Qian, Han alone gave him a farewell gift, deepening Jin's hatred.

sentences.zh: 明年二月假銑等獄詞，謫瀚浙江參政。

translations.literal: The next year in the second month, using the wording of Dai Xian's case, Han was demoted to Administrative Commissioner of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: The following second month Jin used Dai Xian's case as a pretext to demote Han to administrative commissioner in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 致仕。

translations.literal: He retired from office.
translations.idiomatic: He retired.

sentences.zh: 旋指為奸黨。

translations.literal: Soon he was labeled a factional criminal.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was branded a member of the illicit faction.

sentences.zh: 瑾誅，復官，致仕。

translations.literal: When Jin was executed his office was restored and he retired.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin's fall his rank was restored and he retired again.

sentences.zh: 予月廩歲隸如故事。

translations.literal: He was granted monthly grain and annual attendants as of old.
translations.idiomatic: He received the usual retired stipend and attendants.

sentences.zh: 尋命有司歲時存問。

translations.literal: Before long he was ordered to receive seasonal visits from local officials.
translations.idiomatic: Officials were ordered to visit him at the seasons.

sentences.zh: 瀚為人謙厚，而自守介然。

translations.literal: Han as a man was humble and generous, yet in self-preservation he was uncompromising.
translations.idiomatic: He was modest in manner yet rigid in principle.

sentences.zh: 卒年八十六。

translations.literal: He died aged eighty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died at eighty-six.

sentences.zh: 贈太子太保，謚文安。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent with the title Wen'an.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made grand preceptor of the heir apparent with the title Wen'an, meaning Secure in Culture.

sentences.zh: 子九人，庭㭿、庭機最顯。

translations.literal: He had nine sons; Ting'ang and Tingji were most prominent.
translations.idiomatic: Of his nine sons, Ting'ang and Tingji achieved the greatest fame.

sentences.zh: 庭㭿，字利瞻。

translations.literal: Ting'ang, style name Lizhan.
translations.idiomatic: Ting'ang, whose style name was Lizhan.

sentences.zh: 瀚次子也。

translations.literal: He was Han's second son.
translations.idiomatic: He was Han's second son.

sentences.zh: 弘治十二年進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the twelfth year of Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He qualified as jinshi in the twelfth year of Hongzhi.

sentences.zh: 授兵部主事。

translations.literal: He was appointed principal secretary in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was made principal secretary in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 歷職方郎中。

translations.literal: He served through the rank of Director in the Bureau of Operations.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to director in the Bureau of Operations.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書張彩欲改為御史，固謝之，乃以為蘇州知府。

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel Zhang Cai wished to transfer him to censor; he firmly declined, and was therefore made Prefect of Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cai, minister of personnel, wanted to make him a censor; he refused firmly and was appointed prefect of Suzhou instead.

sentences.zh: 頻歲大水，疏請停織造，罷繁征，割關課備振。

translations.literal: For successive years there were great floods; he memorialized requesting a halt to imperial weaving, an end to heavy levies, and diversion of transit duties for relief.
translations.idiomatic: After repeated floods he urged stopping palace weaving, ending oppressive taxes, and diverting transit duties to relief.

sentences.zh: 再上，始報可。

translations.literal: He submitted again before approval was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Only on a second memorial did the court agree.

sentences.zh: 遷雲南左參政。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Left Administrative Commissioner of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to left administrative commissioner of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 正德九年，以父老乞侍養。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Zhengde he begged to nurse his aged father.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Zhengde he asked leave to care for his elderly father.

sentences.zh: 時子炫已成進士，官禮部主事，亦謁假歸。

translations.literal: At the time his son Xuan had already become a jinshi and served as principal secretary in the Ministry of Rites; he too took leave to return.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xuan, already a jinshi and a principal secretary in the Ministry of Rites, also took leave to return home.

sentences.zh: 三世一堂，鄉人稱盛事。

translations.literal: Three generations in one hall—the villagers called it a grand occasion.
translations.idiomatic: Three generations gathered under one roof, which neighbors hailed as a rare family joy.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖初，父憂，服闋，起官江西，歷湖廣左、右布政使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jiajing, after his father's mourning and when mourning ended, he took office in Jiangxi and served as Left and Right Provincial Administration Commissioner of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jiajing, after mourning his father, he served in Jiangxi and rose to left and right administration commissioner of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 舉治行卓異，擢右副都御史，巡撫保定諸府。

translations.literal: Because his governance was outstanding he was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-chief and toured and pacified the prefectures of Baoding.
translations.idiomatic: Recognized for outstanding administration, he became right vice censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Baoding.

sentences.zh: 歷工部右侍郎。

translations.literal: He served as Right Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He became right vice minister of works.

sentences.zh: 應詔言郊壇大工，南城、西苑相繼興作，請以儉約先天下。

translations.literal: In response to an edict on the great suburban altar works, with the southern city and Western Park being built in succession, he asked that frugality lead the empire.
translations.idiomatic: When the court launched major suburban, southern-city, and Western Park projects, he urged the emperor to model frugality for the realm.

sentences.zh: 又因災傷，乞撤還采木、燒造諸使。

translations.literal: Moreover because of disaster and hardship he begged to recall the timber-gathering and porcelain-firing missions.
translations.idiomatic: Citing disaster and hardship, he also asked to recall timber and porcelain missions.

sentences.zh: 進左，拜尚書，加太子太保。

translations.literal: He was advanced to the left, appointed Minister, and given the title Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to left vice minister, then minister, and grand preceptor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 時帝方大興土木功，庭㭿所規畫多稱意。

translations.literal: At the time the emperor was greatly promoting construction; Ting'ang's plans mostly pleased him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was launching vast building projects, and Ting'ang's proposals often pleased him.

sentences.zh: 會詔建沙河行宮，庭㭿議加天下田賦，為御史桑喬、給事中管見所劾。

translations.literal: When an edict ordered a traveling palace at Shahe, Ting'ang proposed increasing the land tax throughout the empire; he was impeached by Censor Sang Qiao and Supervising Secretary Guan Jian.
translations.idiomatic: When a palace was ordered at Shahe, Ting'ang proposed raising land taxes empire-wide and was attacked by Sang Qiao and Guan Jian.

sentences.zh: 乞罷，歸卒，贈少保，謚康懿。

translations.literal: He begged to resign, returned home, and died; he was posthumously made Junior Guardian with the title Kangyi.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned, died at home, and was posthumously made junior guardian with the title Kangyi, meaning Peaceful and Virtuous.

sentences.zh: 炫終通政司參議。

translations.literal: Xuan ended as Vice Commissioner in the Office of Transmission.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan rose to vice commissioner in the Office of Transmission.

sentences.zh: 庭機，字利仁，瀚季子也。

translations.literal: Tingji, style name Liren, was Han's youngest son.
translations.idiomatic: Tingji, style name Liren, was Han's youngest son.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十四年進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the fourteenth year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in the fourteenth year of Jiajing.

sentences.zh: 改庶吉士，授檢討，遷司業，擢南京祭酒，累遷至工部尚書。

translations.literal: He was made a Hanlin Bachelor and appointed Reviser, transferred to Vice-Chancellor, promoted to Nanjing Chancellor, and rose in steps to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He became a Hanlin Bachelor, reviser, vice chancellor, Nanjing chancellor, and eventually minister of works.

sentences.zh: 穆宗立，調禮部，俱官陪京。

translations.literal: When the Muzong Emperor ascended, he was transferred to the Ministry of Rites; both offices were held in the secondary capital.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Muzong he was transferred to the Ministry of Rites while retaining his Nanjing post.

sentences.zh: 時子燫已為祭酒，遂致仕歸。

translations.literal: At the time his son Xun was already chancellor, so he retired.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xun was already chancellor, so he retired.

sentences.zh: 萬歷九年卒，年七十有六。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Wanli he died, aged seventy-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the ninth year of Wanli at seventy-six.

sentences.zh: 贈太子太保，謚文僖。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent with the title Wenxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made grand preceptor of the heir apparent with the title Wenxi, meaning Cultivated and Joyful.

sentences.zh: 子燫、烴。

translations.literal: His sons were Xun and Xuen.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Xun and Xuen.

sentences.zh: 燫，字貞恒，庭機長子。

translations.literal: Xun, style name Zhenheng, was Tingji's eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: Xun, style name Zhenheng, was Tingji's eldest son.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二十六進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the twenty-sixth year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: He qualified as jinshi in the twenty-sixth year of Jiajing.

sentences.zh: 改庶吉士，授檢討。

translations.literal: He was made a Hanlin Bachelor and appointed Reviser.
translations.idiomatic: He became a Hanlin Bachelor and reviser.

sentences.zh: 景恭王就邸，命燫侍講讀。

translations.literal: When Prince Jinggong took up his fief, Xun was ordered to attend him in study and reading.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Jinggong went to his estate, Xun was assigned to tutor him.

sentences.zh: 三遷國子祭酒。

translations.literal: He was transferred three times to Chancellor of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: He was thrice promoted to university chancellor.

sentences.zh: 自燫祖瀚，父庭機，三世為祭酒，前此未有也。

translations.literal: From Xun's grandfather Han and father Tingji, three generations were chancellors—never before seen.
translations.idiomatic: With his grandfather Han and father Tingji, three generations held the chancellorship—an unprecedented honor.

sentences.zh: 隆度改元，擢禮部右侍郎，充日講官。

translations.literal: When the Longqing reign title was adopted, he was promoted to Vice Minister of Rites and served as daily lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Longqing he was made vice minister of rites and daily lecturer.

sentences.zh: 寇犯邊，條上備邊七事。

translations.literal: When bandits raided the border he itemized seven border-defense measures.
translations.idiomatic: When raiders struck the frontier he submitted seven proposals for border defense.

sentences.zh: 改吏部，調南京吏部，署禮部事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel, then to Nanjing Ministry of Personnel, and acted in Ministry of Rites affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He moved to the Ministry of Personnel, then to its Nanjing counterpart, while acting in rites.

sentences.zh: 魏國公徐鵬舉廢長立幼，燫持不可。

translations.literal: Duke of Wei Xu Pengju wished to depose the elder and establish the younger; Xun held that this could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: When the Duke of Wei sought to disinherit an elder son for a younger, Xun refused to approve.

sentences.zh: 萬歷元年進工部尚書，改禮部。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wanli he was advanced to Minister of Works and transferred to the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Wanli he became minister of works, then minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 仍居南京。

translations.literal: He still resided in Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He remained in Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 名位一與父庭機等。

translations.literal: In fame and rank he was equal to his father Tingji.
translations.idiomatic: His rank and reputation matched his father Tingji's.

sentences.zh: 母喪去官。

translations.literal: He left office on his mother's death.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 服闋，以庭機篤老侍養，家居七年，先父庭機卒。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, because Tingji was aged and devoted he nursed him at home for seven years; his father Tingji died before him.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he cared for the aged Tingji at home for seven years until his father's death.

sentences.zh: 贈太子少保，謚文恪。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent with the title Wenke.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made junior guardian of the heir apparent with the title Wenke, meaning Cultivated and Reverent.

sentences.zh: 明代三世為尚書，並得謚文。

translations.literal: In the Ming, three generations as ministers all receiving posthumous titles with Wen—
translations.idiomatic: In the Ming only one family produced three generations of ministers all bearing posthumous titles with the character wen—

sentences.zh: 林氏一家而已。

translations.literal: only the Lin clan.
translations.idiomatic: the Lin family alone.

sentences.zh: 子世勤，性篤孝。

translations.literal: His son Shiqin was by nature deeply filial.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shiqin was profoundly filial.

sentences.zh: 芝生者三，枯篁復青。

translations.literal: Three lingzhi fungi grew; withered bamboo turned green again.
translations.idiomatic: Three lingzhi mushrooms appeared and withered bamboo sprouted green again.

sentences.zh: 御史上其事，被旌。

translations.literal: A censor reported the matter and he received an imperial commendation.
translations.idiomatic: A censor reported the prodigy and the court honored him.

sentences.zh: 烴字貞燿，庭機次子也。

translations.literal: Xuen, style name Zhenyao, was Tingji's second son.
translations.idiomatic: Xuen, style name Zhenyao, was Tingji's second son.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖四十一年進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the forty-first year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in the forty-first year of Jiajing.

sentences.zh: 授戶部主事，歷廣西副使。

translations.literal: He was appointed principal secretary in the Ministry of Revenue and served as Vice Commissioner of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was made principal secretary in the Ministry of Revenue and rose to vice commissioner of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 兄燫卒，請急歸養。

translations.literal: When his elder brother Xun died he requested urgent leave to nurse his kin.
translations.idiomatic: When Xun died he hurried home on compassionate leave.

sentences.zh: 久之，歷太僕少卿。

translations.literal: After a long time he served as Junior Director of the Court of Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: Later he became junior director of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 因災異極陳礦稅之害，請釋逮系諸臣。

translations.literal: Because of calamities and anomalies he urgently set forth the harm of mining taxes and begged release of imprisoned officials.
translations.idiomatic: Citing omens and disasters, he denounced mining taxes and asked to free imprisoned officials.

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: No reply was given.
translations.idiomatic: The court did not respond.

sentences.zh: 終南京工部尚書致仕。

translations.literal: He ended as Minister of Works in Nanjing and retired.
translations.idiomatic: He retired as minister of works in Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 林氏三世五尚書，皆內行修潔，為時所稱。

translations.literal: The Lin clan for three generations had five ministers, all upright in private conduct and praised by the age.
translations.idiomatic: Three generations of the Lin family produced five ministers, all noted for personal integrity.

sentences.zh: 謝鐸，字鳴治，浙江太平人。

translations.literal: Xie Duo, style name Mingzhi, was a native of Taiping in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Duo, whose style name was Mingzhi, came from Taiping in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 天順末進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi at the end of Tianshun.
translations.idiomatic: He qualified as a jinshi late in the Tianshun reign.

sentences.zh: 改庶吉士，授編修，預修《英宗實錄》。

translations.literal: He was made a Hanlin Bachelor and appointed Compiler, and took part in compiling the Veritable Records of Yingzong.
translations.idiomatic: He became a Hanlin Bachelor and compiler and helped compile the Veritable Records of the Yingzong Emperor.

sentences.zh: 性介特，力學慕古，講求經世務。

translations.literal: His nature was peculiar and upright; he studied hard and admired antiquity, seeking practical statecraft.
translations.idiomatic: Upright and solitary by nature, he studied the classics and pursued practical statecraft.

sentences.zh: 成化九年校勘《通鑒綱目》，上言：「《綱目》一書，帝王龜鑒。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Chenghua he collated the Outline and Details of the Comprehensive Mirror and memorialized: "The Outline and Details is a tortoise mirror for emperors.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Chenghua, while collating the Outline and Details of the Comprehensive Mirror, he wrote: "This book is the emperor's mirror of governance.

sentences.zh: 陛下命重加考定，必將進講經筵，為致治資也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has ordered a renewed examination; it will surely be brought to the Classics Colloquium and serve as material for bringing order.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has ordered a new recension; it should be lectured at court as a guide to good government.

sentences.zh: 今天下有太平之形，無太平之實，因仍積習，廢實徇名。

translations.literal: Today the empire has the form of peace but not the reality; old habits persist, empty names are pursued while substance is abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: The realm looks peaceful but is not; empty formalism and neglect of substance persist.

sentences.zh: 曰振綱紀，而小人無畏忌；

translations.literal: It is said to restore discipline, yet petty men have no fear;
translations.idiomatic: We claim to restore discipline, yet petty men act without fear;

sentences.zh: 曰勵風俗，而縉紳棄廉恥。

translations.literal: it is said to encourage custom, yet gentry and officials cast aside integrity and shame.
translations.idiomatic: we claim to encourage morals, yet officials abandon integrity and shame.

sentences.zh: 飭官司，而汙暴益甚；

translations.literal: Officials are disciplined, yet corruption grows worse;
translations.idiomatic: We discipline the bureaucracy, yet corruption worsens;

sentences.zh: 恤軍民，而罷敝益極。

translations.literal: soldiers and people are comforted, yet exhaustion reaches its extreme.
translations.idiomatic: we comfort troops and civilians, yet their exhaustion deepens.

sentences.zh: 減省有制，而興作每疲於奔命；

translations.literal: There are rules for reduction and economy, yet construction projects constantly wear people out running about;
translations.idiomatic: Statutes limit spending, yet construction still drives men to exhaustion;

sentences.zh: 蠲免有詔，而征斂每困於追呼。

translations.literal: there are edicts for exemption, yet collection constantly traps people in the press of demands.
translations.idiomatic: tax relief is proclaimed, yet collectors still hound the people.

sentences.zh: 考察非不舉，而幸門日開；

translations.literal: Inspections are not neglected, yet doors of favor open daily;
translations.idiomatic: Inspections continue, yet back doors to favor multiply;

sentences.zh: 簡練非不行，而私撓日眾。

translations.literal: training is not unimplemented, yet private interference grows daily.
translations.idiomatic: military training proceeds, yet private meddling grows.

sentences.zh: 賞竭府庫之財，而有功者不勸；

translations.literal: Rewards exhaust the treasury yet those with merit are not encouraged;
translations.idiomatic: Rewards drain the treasury without encouraging merit;

sentences.zh: 罰窮讞覆之案，而有罪者不懲。

translations.literal: punishments exhaust cases in the review office yet those with guilt are not punished.
translations.idiomatic: punishments pile up without disciplining the guilty.

sentences.zh: 以至修省祈禱之命屢頒，水旱災傷之來不絕。

translations.literal: To the point that orders for self-examination and prayer are repeatedly issued, while floods, drought, and disasters never cease.
translations.idiomatic: Edicts for repentance multiply, yet flood, drought, and disaster never cease.

sentences.zh: 禁垣被震，城門示災，不思疏動旋轉，以大答天人之望，是則誠可憂也。

translations.literal: The palace quarters were struck by earthquake, the city gate showed omens of disaster—yet there is no thought of easing movement and turning round to answer heaven and men's hopes in a great way; this is truly worrisome.
translations.idiomatic: Earthquakes shook the palace and omens appeared at the gates, yet the court will not change course to answer heaven and the people—this is truly alarming.

sentences.zh: 願陛下以古證今，兢兢業業，然後可長治久安，而載籍不為無用矣。」

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty to test the present by antiquity, cautious and fearful, and then long peace and stability can be achieved and the records will not be useless.
translations.idiomatic: I urge Your Majesty to measure the present against antiquity, act with caution and reverence, secure lasting peace, and make these books live again.

sentences.zh: 帝不能從。

translations.literal: The emperor could not follow it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not heed him.

sentences.zh: 時塞上有警，條上備邊事宜，請養兵積粟，收復東勝、河套故疆。
