translations.literal: At the time there was alarm on the frontier; he itemized border-defense measures, requesting to nourish troops and store grain and recover the old territories of East Sheng and the Ordos.
translations.idiomatic: When the frontier was threatened he urged training troops, stockpiling grain, and recovering East Sheng and the Ordos.

sentences.zh: 又言：「今之邊將，無異晚唐債帥。

translations.literal: He also said: "Today's border generals are no different from the debt-commanders of late Tang.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "Today's frontier generals are no better than the debt-ridden commanders of late Tang.

sentences.zh: 敗則士卒受其殃，捷則權豪蒙其賞。

translations.literal: When defeated the soldiers bear the calamity; when victorious powerful families receive the reward.
translations.idiomatic: Defeat falls on the rank and file; victory enriches powerful families.

sentences.zh: 且克侵軍餉，辦納月錢，三軍方怨憤填膺，孰肯為國效命者？」

translations.literal: Moreover they encroach on military pay and collect monthly fees; the three armies are just filling with resentment—who is willing to die for the state?
translations.idiomatic: They embezzle pay and levy monthly fees until the armies seethe with resentment—who will fight for the state?

sentences.zh: 語皆切時弊。

translations.literal: His words all cut the ailments of the time.
translations.idiomatic: Every word struck at contemporary abuses.

sentences.zh: 秩滿，進侍講，直經筵。

translations.literal: When his term was complete he was advanced to Lecturer and attended the Classics Colloquium.
translations.idiomatic: When his term expired he became lecturer at the imperial colloquium.

sentences.zh: 遭兩喪，服除，以親不逮養，遂不起。

translations.literal: He suffered two bereavements; when mourning ended, because his parents had not enjoyed his support in life, he did not take office again.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning both parents he declined further office, grieved that he had not supported them in life.

sentences.zh: 弘治初，言者交薦，以原官召修《憲宗實錄》。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Hongzhi memorialists repeatedly recommended him; he was summoned in his former rank to compile the Veritable Records of Xianzong.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Hongzhi he was repeatedly recommended and recalled to compile the Veritable Records of Xianzong.

sentences.zh: 三年擢南京國子祭酒。

translations.literal: In the third year he was promoted to Chancellor of the Nanjing National University.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was made chancellor of the Nanjing Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 上言六事，曰擇師儒，慎科貢，正祀典，廣載籍，復會饌，均撥歷。

translations.literal: He memorialized on six matters: selecting teachers, careful examination candidates, correcting sacrificial canon, broadening libraries, restoring communal feasts, and equalizing practical assignments.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed six reforms: better teachers, stricter examinations, corrected ritual canon, expanded libraries, restored communal feasts, and fairer practical assignments.

sentences.zh: 其正祀典，請進宋儒楊時而罷吳澄。

translations.literal: In correcting sacrificial canon he asked to advance the Song scholar Yang Shi and remove Wu Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: On ritual canon he urged elevating the Song scholar Yang Shi and demoting Wu Cheng.

sentences.zh: 禮部尚書傅瀚持之，乃進時而澄祀如故。

translations.literal: Minister of Rites Fu Han held to the old view; in the end Shi was advanced while Cheng's worship remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Fu Han resisted; Yang Shi was advanced but Wu Cheng's place in the temple remained.

sentences.zh: 明年謝病去。

translations.literal: The next year he resigned on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he resigned for illness.

sentences.zh: 家居將十年，薦者益眾。

translations.literal: At home for nearly ten years, those who recommended him grew ever more numerous.
translations.idiomatic: At home nearly ten years, recommendations multiplied.

sentences.zh: 會國子缺祭酒，部議起之。

translations.literal: When the National University lacked a chancellor, the ministry deliberated on recalling him.
translations.idiomatic: When the university needed a chancellor, the ministry proposed recalling him.

sentences.zh: 帝素重鐸，擢禮部右侍郎，管祭酒事。

translations.literal: The emperor had always valued Duo and promoted him to Vice Minister of Rites while directing chancellor affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor esteemed Duo and made him vice minister of rites while he continued as chancellor.

sentences.zh: 屢辭，不許。

translations.literal: He repeatedly declined; it was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He declined repeatedly but was overruled.

sentences.zh: 時章懋為南祭酒，兩人皆人師，諸生交相慶。

translations.literal: At the time Zhang Mao was Nanjing chancellor; both were teachers of men and the students congratulated one another.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Mao was Nanjing chancellor; students rejoiced to have two master teachers at once.

sentences.zh: 居五年，引疾歸。

translations.literal: After five years he cited illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: After five years he retired again on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 鐸經術湛深，為文章有體要。

translations.literal: Duo's classical learning was profound; in writing he had structure and essentials.
translations.idiomatic: His classical learning was profound and his prose disciplined.

sentences.zh: 兩為國子師，嚴課程，杜請謁，增號舍，修堂室，擴廟門。

translations.literal: Twice teacher at the National University, he strictly enforced the curriculum, blocked private petitions, increased dormitory rooms, repaired halls, and expanded the temple gate.
translations.idiomatic: Twice university chancellor, he tightened the curriculum, barred favor-seeking, expanded dormitories, repaired halls, and widened the temple gate.

sentences.zh: 置公廨三十余居其屬。

translations.literal: He established more than thirty official residences for his staff.
translations.idiomatic: He built more than thirty official residences for his staff.

sentences.zh: 諸生貧者周恤之，死者請官定制為之殮。

translations.literal: Poor students he aided; for the dead he requested official regulations for burial.
translations.idiomatic: He aided poor students and secured official funeral rites for those who died.

sentences.zh: 家居好周恤族黨，自奉則布衣蔬食。

translations.literal: At home he gladly aided his clan; for himself he wore plain cloth and ate vegetables.
translations.idiomatic: In retirement he supported his clan generously while living on plain food and coarse cloth.

sentences.zh: 正德五年卒。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhengde he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifth year of Zhengde.

sentences.zh: 贈禮部尚書，謚文肅。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Minister of Rites with the title Wensu.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made minister of rites with the title Wensu, meaning Cultivated and Solemn.

sentences.zh: 魯鐸，字振之，景陵人。

translations.literal: Lu Duo, style name Zhenzhi, was a native of Jingling.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Duo, whose style name was Zhenzhi, came from Jingling.

sentences.zh: 弘治十五年會試第一。

translations.literal: First place in the metropolitan examination in the fifteenth year of Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He ranked first in the metropolitan examination in the fifteenth year of Hongzhi.

sentences.zh: 歷編修。

translations.literal: He served as Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He served as compiler.

sentences.zh: 閉門自守，不妄交人。

translations.literal: He shut his door and kept himself, not making acquaintances lightly.
translations.idiomatic: He kept to himself and made few acquaintances.

sentences.zh: 武宗立，使安南，卻其饋。

translations.literal: When the Wuzong Emperor ascended he was sent to Annam and refused their gifts.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wuzong took the throne he was envoy to Annam and refused bribes.

sentences.zh: 正德二年遷國子監司業。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhengde he was transferred to Vice-Chancellor of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhengde he became vice chancellor of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 累擢南祭酒，尋改北。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Nanjing Chancellor and soon transferred to Beijing.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Nanjing chancellor, then moved to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 鐸屢典成均，教士切實為學，不專章句。

translations.literal: Duo several times directed the Imperial Academy; in teaching scholars he urged solid learning, not specializing in commentarial phrases alone.
translations.idiomatic: Often head of the academy, he taught practical learning rather than mere exegesis.

sentences.zh: 士有假歸廢學者，訓飭之，悔過乃已。

translations.literal: If scholars on leave abandoned study, he admonished them and only stopped when they repented.
translations.idiomatic: Students who neglected study on leave were rebuked until they repented.

sentences.zh: 久之，謝病歸。

translations.literal: After a long time he resigned on grounds of illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Eventually he retired ill to his home.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖初，以刑部尚書林俊薦，用孝宗朝謝鐸故事，起南祭酒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jiajing, on Minister of Justice Lin Jun's recommendation, following the precedent of Xie Duo in the Xiaozong reign, he was recalled as Nanjing Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jiajing, Lin Jun recommended recalling him as Nanjing chancellor, as Xie Duo had been under Xiaozong.

sentences.zh: 逾年，復請致仕。

translations.literal: After more than a year he again requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he again asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 累征不起，卒。

translations.literal: Repeated summonses he did not answer; he died.
translations.idiomatic: Further summons went unanswered until his death.

sentences.zh: 謚文恪。

translations.literal: Posthumous title Wenke.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted the posthumous title Wenke, meaning Cultivated and Reverent.

sentences.zh: 鐸以德望重於時。

translations.literal: Duo was respected in the age for moral stature.
translations.idiomatic: His moral authority was widely respected.

sentences.zh: 居鄉，有盜掠牛馬，或紿云：「魯祭酒物也」，舍之去。

translations.literal: Living in his district, when bandits plundered cattle and horses some would deceive them saying "These are Chancellor Lu's goods," and they would leave them and go.
translations.idiomatic: At home, thieves who learned goods belonged to Chancellor Lu often left them untouched.

sentences.zh: 大學士李東陽生日，鐸為司業，與祭酒趙永皆其門生也，相約以二帕為壽。

translations.literal: On Grand Secretary Li Dongyang's birthday, Duo was Vice-Chancellor and Chancellor Zhao Yong were both his pupils; they agreed to take two bolts of silk as a birthday gift.
translations.idiomatic: For Grand Secretary Li Dongyang's birthday, Duo as vice chancellor and Zhao Yong as chancellor—both his students—agreed to bring two bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 比檢笥，亡有，徐曰：「鄉有饋乾魚者，盍以此往？」

translations.literal: When they checked the chest there was none; he said slowly: "In the village someone presented dried fish—why not take that?
translations.idiomatic: Finding none in the chest, Duo said: "Someone sent dried fish from the village—shall we bring that instead?

sentences.zh: 詢諸庖，食過半矣，以其余詣東陽。

translations.literal: He asked the kitchen; more than half had been eaten; with the remainder they went to Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: The kitchen had already eaten half; they took the rest to Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 東陽喜，為烹魚置酒，留二人飲，極歡乃去。

translations.literal: Dongyang was pleased, cooked the fish and set out wine, kept the two to drink, and only when extremely happy did they leave.
translations.idiomatic: Dongyang delighted, cooked the fish, poured wine, and kept them in merry conversation until night.

sentences.zh: 永，字爾錫，臨淮人。

translations.literal: Yong, style name Erxi, was a native of Linhuai.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yong, style name Erxi, came from Linhuai.

sentences.zh: 與鐸同年進士，亦官編修。

translations.literal: He and Duo were jinshi in the same year; he also served as Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He and Duo qualified as jinshi the same year and both became compilers.

sentences.zh: 復與鐸相繼為祭酒。

translations.literal: Again he and Duo in succession were chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: He and Duo later served in turn as chancellor.

sentences.zh: 尋遷南京禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Vice Minister of Rites in Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made vice minister of rites in Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 大學士楊一清重其才，欲引以自助，乃為他語挑之。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Yang Yiqing valued his talent and wished to draw him to assist himself; he therefore probed him with other words.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Yang Yiqing admired him and tried to draw him into his faction with hints.

sentences.zh: 永正色曰：「可以纓冠汙吾道乎？」

translations.literal: Yong said with a stern face: "Can the official cap and belt be used to defile my Way?
translations.idiomatic: Yong replied sternly: "Would you stain my integrity with an official appointment?

sentences.zh: 遂請致仕去。

translations.literal: Thereupon he requested retirement and left.
translations.idiomatic: He at once petitioned to retire.

sentences.zh: 人服其廉介。

translations.literal: People admired his integrity.
translations.idiomatic: All admired his probity.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：明太祖時，國學師儒，體貌優重。

translations.literal: The comment says: In the time of Ming Taizu, teachers at the Imperial Academy received preferential treatment in bearing and status.
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: Under the founding emperor, Imperial University teachers enjoyed exceptional honor.

sentences.zh: 魏觀、宋訥為祭酒，造就人才，克舉其職。

translations.literal: Wei Guan and Song Na as chancellors molded talent and fully performed their duties.
translations.idiomatic: As chancellors, Wei Guan and Song Na trained talent and fulfilled their roles.

sentences.zh: 諸生銜命奉使，往往擢為大官，不專以科目進也。

translations.literal: Students bearing orders on missions were often promoted to high office; advancement was not solely through the examination track.
translations.idiomatic: Students sent on missions often rose to high office without relying solely on examinations.

sentences.zh: 中葉以還，流品稍雜，撥歷亦為具文，成均師席，不過為儒臣序遷之地而已。

translations.literal: From the mid-dynasty onward the stream of ranks grew somewhat mixed; practical assignments also became empty form; the master's seat at the Imperial Academy was no more than a place in the orderly promotion of scholar-officials.
translations.idiomatic: By mid-dynasty ranks grew mixed and practical training became nominal; the chancellorship was merely another step for literati.

sentences.zh: 李時勉、陳敬宗諸人，方廉清鯁，表範卓然，類而傳之，庶觀者有所法焉。

translations.literal: Li Shimian, Chen Jingzong, and the others were upright, pure, and stern, with outstanding models; if grouped and transmitted, perhaps observers would have something to emulate.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Li Shimian, Chen Jingzong, and their peers were upright exemplars; recorded together, they might still teach later ages.
